label: Lessons from the past
title: Give the clinical study a biological question to answer.
intro: Before a study, define what your measurements can establish and why the proposed patients are informative. Then use clinical findings to refine the hypothesis. These three FDA records show that sequence.

sequence.label: Interpret the drug effect
sequence.title: A measurable drug effect is not yet a demonstrated benefit.
sequence.preview: PTH fell. Had bone disease improved?
sequence.provenance: Reproduced in the 2004 approval package. Earlier human studies already existed; this US IND proposed a Phase 2 study.
sequence.question: What did lowering parathyroid hormone actually establish?
sequence.setup: Cinacalcet increases the calcium sensitivity of parathyroid cells. In secondary hyperparathyroidism, the rationale was that lowering excess parathyroid hormone (PTH) could improve bone disease.

visual.label: Separate drug action, measured response, and expected benefit

nodes.label: Drug action
nodes.title: Increase calcium sensitivity
nodes.text: Change the signal controlling PTH secretion.

nodes.label: Observed response
nodes.title: PTH decreases
nodes.text: Reported in rats and earlier healthy-volunteer studies.

nodes.label: Benefit to establish
nodes.title: Improve bone disease
nodes.text: An expectation in these review pages, not an established outcome.

decision.label: The proposed next study
decision.text: Study patients with secondary hyperparathyroidism and measure PTH, calcium, calcitonin, and PK. Calcium mattered for safety as well as pharmacology.

lesson.label: Use this distinction
lesson.text: A pharmacodynamic readout can show a drug effect. Separate that observation from the evidence needed to show that patients benefit.

sequence.limit: These passages do not establish improved bone disease or fracture prevention. An original US IND is not necessarily a first-ever human study.

sources.label: FDA · original IND rationale and study plan, PDF 8–9

sequence.label: Justify who to study
sequence.title: Broad enrollment can still have a specific biological hypothesis.
sequence.preview: Who should enter—and what would their results tell us?
sequence.provenance: The 2025 approval package reproduces later IND correspondence recounting the 2011 pre-IND advice and early clinical development.
sequence.question: How can a broad dose-escalation study test a targeted-drug hypothesis?
sequence.setup: The pre-IND discussion considered possible activity in tumors with ALK or cMET alterations. FDA addressed patient enrollment and pharmacodynamic measurements as separate planning questions.

visual.label: Two complementary questions in the pre-IND advice

nodes.label: Patient selection
nodes.title: Who enters?
nodes.text: Specify how many patients negative for both ALK and cMET would be enrolled.

nodes.label: PK and pharmacodynamics
nodes.title: What can we measure?
nodes.text: Plan PK sampling and identify potential PD endpoints.

visual.note: Patient characteristics frame who might benefit. PK and PD measurements help interpret exposure and biological effects after dosing. These are different jobs.

decision.label: How the study later developed
decision.text: The 2014 account describes advanced-solid-tumor dose escalation followed by expansion in ALK-positive non-small cell lung cancer, selected by FISH testing.

lesson.label: Use this distinction
lesson.text: A patient hypothesis need not mean restricting every cohort to one marker. Explain what each enrolled group and each measurement will help you learn.

sequence.limit: The record does not give the requested marker-negative enrollment number. The 2014 expansion design should not be assumed to have been present in the original March 2012 protocol.

sources.label: FDA · pre-IND advice and early study design, PDF 49–50

sequence.label: Refine the hypothesis
sequence.title: Early findings can change which patients you study next.
sequence.preview: An ALK-positive signal led to a narrower clinical question.
sequence.provenance: Development history reconstructed in the 2011 NDA clinical review; this is not the complete original IND submission.
sequence.question: What should happen when patients reveal a more specific opportunity?
sequence.setup: Crizotinib entered broad cancer dose escalation as a c-Met/HGFR inhibitor. FDA’s later account links observations in two ALK-positive lung-cancer patients to an ALK-positive extension of the study.

visual.label: From broad dose escalation to an ALK-positive extension

nodes.label: Original study
nodes.title: Broad cancer enrollment
nodes.text: Dose escalation in advanced cancers, excluding leukemia.

nodes.label: Early observation
nodes.title: Two ALK-positive patients
nodes.text: In the 50 mg cohort, stable disease was reported at 1.5 and 7 months.

nodes.label: October 2007 amendment
nodes.title: Test ALK-positive NSCLC
nodes.text: The protocol allowed enrollment of EML4–ALK-positive non-small cell lung cancer.

decision.label: What changed
decision.text: An ALK-positive extension tested the emerging population hypothesis. A later 2009 amendment also added an ALK-negative cohort.

lesson.label: Use this distinction
lesson.text: An early signal can justify a more focused test before it establishes that a marker predicts benefit. Build a plan that can change when the evidence changes.

sequence.limit: These were stable-disease observations, not objective responses or proof of benefit. The retrospective account does not establish every measurement in the original protocol.

sources.label: FDA · early observations and protocol amendments, PDF 37–38

takeaway.title: Bring a hypothesis—and a way to learn.
takeaway.text: Know what your measurements can establish. Explain why the proposed patients are informative. Decide what findings would strengthen, narrow, or change the hypothesis.
takeaway.note: These cases illustrate scientific decisions, not a universal biomarker requirement or a complete checklist for an IND.

archive.label: Explore the full case collection
archive.intro: For deeper reading: additional drugs, contrasting findings, and later development decisions. Each case identifies its source stage; later approval findings should not be read as initial-IND requirements.
